stem: According to Garrison’s observations, how were slaves and free blacks treated similarly in both the North and the South?
instruction: Read the excerpt and answer the question that follows.

options.label: A
options.text: Both slaves and free blacks could travel without restrictions.

options.label: B
options.text: Both slaves and free blacks experienced discrimination.

options.label: C
options.text: Both slaves and free blacks often owned businesses.

options.label: D
options.text: Both slaves and free blacks were not paid for their work.

visual_elements: In most of the States in which slavery is tolerated, the laws in relation to free [black] persons are severe in the extreme. Though their freedom is recognized, yet they have not the rights of other freemen. . . . At the North, few blacks are mechanics, because the whites will not allow them to work with them. At the South, on the contrary, few of the mechanics are whites, because they will not do the same sort of work as blacks. —William Lloyd Garrison, The Liberator, January 22, 1831
